chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a man who had struck another man until his eyesight was diminished. So he called men of his age, then showed them something, and he examined how much of his eyesight had diminished; then he gave him the blood money for the amount by which his eyesight had diminished.

key_terms.أَسْنَانِهِ: those of similar age, used here for comparison in assessment
key_terms.أَمِيرُ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلسَّلَا: Commander of the Faithful, Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام, acting here as judge
key_terms.دِيَةَ مَا ٱنْتَقَصَ مِنْ بَصَرِهِ: financial compensation proportionate to the amount of eyesight lost
key_terms.ٱنْتَقَصَ مِنْ بَصَرِهِ: a reduction or partial loss of eyesight

ai.seo_question: How is blood money determined for partial loss of eyesight in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a judicial ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in a case of bodily injury affecting eyesight. It shows that compensation was assessed proportionally to the measurable loss of vision, establishing a practical method for determining diyyah in partial injury cases.
